title: The Thirsty Hiker
briefing: Priya, 14, is leading her scout troop up a sunny canyon trail. Two hours in she feels dizzy, her mouth is dry, and she hasn't needed a bathroom break all morning.
question: What is her body telling her?

clues.title: Dry mouth and thirst
clues.text: She keeps licking her lips and says she is really thirsty — but not hungry at all.
clues.shows: a strong thirst signal with no hunger

clues.title: Sweaty, hot morning
clues.text: It is 92 °F on the trail. After two hours of climbing her shirt is soaked through with sweat.
clues.shows: a lot of water leaving her body as sweat

clues.title: No bathroom break
clues.text: None since 8 a.m. When she finally goes, there is very little, and it is dark yellow.

clues.title: Better in the shade
clues.text: Ten minutes after two cups of water in the shade, the dizziness fades and she feels like herself again.

hypotheses.text: She is just tired from walking uphill.
hypotheses.flaw: Tiredness from walking does not make you thirsty with a dry mouth, and it would not switch off ten minutes after a drink.

hypotheses.text: She has lost more water (sweat) than she drank, so her body is low on water and is trying to save it.

hypotheses.flaw: A big breakfast would make her feel full, not dizzy and thirsty — and it has nothing to do with sweat or dark pee.

hypotheses.text: The trail is too high and the air is thin.
hypotheses.flaw: A canyon trail is not high enough for thin air, and thin air does not dry your mouth or stop you needing the bathroom.

prediction.prompt: Priya climbs in the heat for three hours, drinking about one cup an hour. What happens to the water level in her body over those three hours?

second.question: And the amount of pee her kidneys make?

concepts.label: more out than in
concepts.hint: Compare what went out with what came in.

concepts.label: kidneys / pee
concepts.hint: Which organ decides how much water to let go?

concepts.label: thirst signal
concepts.hint: How does the body tell her to drink?

concepts.label: drinking fixes it
concepts.hint: What made her feel better, and how fast?

transfer.context: Marco plays a 90-minute soccer match on a hot day. Afterwards he has a headache and his pee is dark yellow.
options: He strained a muscle in his leg.
He sweated out more water than he drank, so his body is low on water.
The sun gave him a sunburn.
transfer.retryHint: Dark yellow pee after a hot game — which of Priya's clues was almost the same?
transfer.explanation: Running for 90 minutes in the heat means a lot of sweat. If Marco drank less than he sweated, his body is low on water: the kidneys save water (dark pee) and the brain signals it (headache, thirst). Same water budget as Priya's.

takeaway: Your body keeps a water budget. When more goes out as sweat than comes in, the kidneys hold water back and the brain turns on thirst — two different signals, one cause.
